problem: isReviewPackageDir hard-codes the package layout (.metaproject/reviews/<id> and .metaproject/flows/<flow>/reviews/<id>) in the premise-answer module, a third encoding of it beside reviewsRoot/flowsRoot in managed.ts:89 and PACKAGE_GLOBS in prior-round.ts:128. commands/automatic-review.ts (the approval policy) now imports this predicate from the answer module.
impact: A change to the package location (a new root, a configurable reviews dir) must be made in three places; if premise-question's copy lags, --prior and carryPremiseDecisions refuse a real package, silently (carry returns []) while the other two accept it. The approval policy depends on an unrelated answer module for a layout fact.
suggested_fix: Move the predicate next to reviewsRoot/flowsRoot (managed.ts or a small package-location module) and build it from those roots; import it from there in premise-question.ts and automatic-review.ts.

problem: answerPremiseQuestion now also owns round-registry re-recording (RegistryOptions with cwd/dir/warn, registryVouchesPackage before the write, recordFinishedRound after). The registry write runs after the decisions lock is released, so it is outside the lock the header (operator-decisions.ts:20-26) says serialises findings.json writers, and the answer module gained a dependency on round-registry.
impact: Low: a concurrent complete/publish records the same registry entry, so the worst case is the later hash winning; but the 'findings.json writers are serialised' contract no longer covers the hash that vouches for that file. Every caller must now remember to pass cwd or the registry silently stays stale (next round runs full).
suggested_fix: Either note in the lock header that the registry entry is re-recorded outside the lock, or make the registry re-record the caller's job (a thin wrapper used by the CLI and the card) so answerPremiseQuestion stays a two-file writer.
evidence: premise-question.ts:164-169 (re-record after recordPremiseDecision returns); round-registry.ts:363 registryVouchesPackage.

problem: The waive card refuses on the string literal id === "premise-decisions" while readiness.ts exports only the message (PREMISE_DECISIONS_NOT_WAIVABLE); the item id and the never-waivable rule are not exported as one unit, so waiveReadiness (readiness.ts:468) and the card each own a copy of the rule.
impact: A future non-waivable item must be added in both places; the card and the CLI can drift.
suggested_fix: Export a NEVER_WAIVABLE map (id to message) from readiness.ts and have both callers read it.

problem: isReviewPackageDir restates the rule for where a review package lives (directly under .metaproject/reviews/ or .metaproject/flows/<flow>/reviews/) that prior-round.ts already owns as PACKAGE_GLOBS (prior-round.ts:128). The predicate is also a generic path check housed in the premise-answer module, and src/commands/automatic-review.ts now imports it from there for the --prior approval.
impact: A change to the package layout (a new location, a rename of the flows tree) needs two edits in two modules; the one that is missed makes --prior accept or refuse a directory the round detector treats the opposite way, which is the SEC2-001 boundary.
suggested_fix: Put one `isReviewPackageDir(dir, projectRoot)` next to PACKAGE_GLOBS in prior-round.ts (or a small review-package-path module) and import it from premise-question.ts and automatic-review.ts.
evidence: premise-question.ts:82-98; prior-round.ts:128; automatic-review.ts import of isReviewPackageDir from ../review/premise-question

problem: touchesOperatorOnly answers two questions under a name that states one: whether a path hits an operator-only name, and (last clause, `!real.startsWith(realDir + sep)`) whether the resolved target escapes the package. A reader of the call site at :323 sees 'not operator-only' and cannot tell it also decides containment. It also resolves symlinks repeatedly: realTarget(resolved) runs at :322 and again inside at :259, and realTarget(dir) at :260 for every approved patch path.
impact: A later edit that narrows the helper to its name (for example to reuse it for a read check) silently drops the containment guard; the repeated filesystem walks are cheap today but hide that the caller and the helper must agree on the same real path.
suggested_fix: Split into `touchesOperatorOnlyName` and `escapesPackage`, compute `real` once in the approval and pass it in; keep the call site reading `inside && dataExtension && !operatorOnly`.
principle: Clean Code G11/N4 (name says one thing), G5

problem: normaliseCarriedPremise grew to five exit paths and three derived flags (stale, stray, stillADowngrade) mixing three rules: strip the operator answer, strip a severity a non-downgrade verdict cannot carry, and re-validate a downgrade against the finding's severity or drop the premise. Each rule is commented in the doc block, but the function body interleaves them.
impact: Adding a verdict or a fourth rule needs reasoning about which early return it must precede; the two `{ ...finding, premise: ... }` branches differ only by which keys are removed.
suggested_fix: Extract `withoutStraySeverity(judgement)` and `downgradeStillHolds(finding, premise)` so the body reads: strip operator; if not downgraded return stripped; if downgrade no longer holds drop the premise; else restamp severity.
principle: Clean Code F3/G30 (one level of abstraction, function does one thing)

problem: answerPremiseQuestion carries a mutable `rerecord` flag that the applyFirst callback sets and the undo closure clears, then is read after recordPremiseDecision returns: control state passed through a captured variable across two closures and a lock boundary. The function also now does four things (apply to findings.json with undo, append the decision, decide whether the registry vouched, re-record and warn).
impact: The invariant 'rerecord is true only when the findings write landed and the decision append did not undo it' lives in three places (assignment at 202, reset at 205, read at 211); a future early return in the callback that forgets the reset leaves the registry re-recording a package whose answer was rolled back.
suggested_fix: Have the callback return `{ undo, vouched }` (or have recordPremiseDecision return what applyFirst returned) so the caller reads one value after the lock instead of a flag mutated by two closures; move the registry step into a small `reRecordRegistry(packageDir, registry)` helper.
principle: Clean Code G36/F3 (flag state across closures, function does one thing)

problem: readPremiseClaimsFile is typed `Promise<ReturnType<typeof parsePremiseClaims>>` while its doc says it returns undefined when there are no claims; the type depends on parsePremiseClaims' return admitting undefined, and `ReturnType<typeof ...>` hides that from the reader. Informational: the rename premiseClaims to premisedFindings in InterimVerdict is complete in src (no stale reader found).
impact: None today; a change to parsePremiseClaims' return type changes this signature silently.
suggested_fix: Name the type: `Promise<ParsedPremiseClaims | undefined>`.

quote: **A flow sourced from a finding: check its premise before freeze.**
problem: The CC2-003 fix went the other way: it removed the heading instead of giving the freeze block one. 'Then freeze and start' with `flow freeze --yes` / `flow start` (:279-284) now belongs to the tasks-gate section (:257-275). The mandatory freeze of every flow reads as the tail of a verification-task section.

quote: comment or commit message giving a reason (`git log -L <start>,<end>:<file>`,
problem: The delta made git conditional on the host (Read-only row, source row :66), but question 1's signal-gathering text (:73-76) still names git log -L, git blame and git show as the method, with no keryx shell fallback.

problem: The same host-git caveat is pasted twice (Purpose sentence and 'Supplied text first') into about 14 reviewer skills, plus the input schema and the orchestrator. The delta lengthened both copies, so the next host-fact edit is 30+ edits across two trees; the law is already named 'law 4'.

quote: "scope: the plan items only. A finding outside them is recorded as follow-up, not fixed in this flow.", "premise: every plan item's comment
problem: The new constraint is appended on the same line as the scope string, while every other element of the constraints array sits on its own line.

problem: If appendDecision throws and the undo (writeFileAtomic of the saved findings.json) also throws, `await undo?.()` raises first and the original append error is lost; findings.json then keeps the applied answer while no decision is recorded.
impact: Needs two consecutive disk write failures in one lock window; the operator sees the undo error, not the cause, and the two files disagree (the state HL2-003 removed).
suggested_fix: Wrap undo in try/catch and rethrow the original error (or an AggregateError naming both).

problem: The registry vouch check and the findings.json write happen inside the lock, but recordFinishedRound re-hashes after the lock is released. An ingest or disposition write landing between the two is hashed into the registry record as if it were the answer's own result.
impact: Registry then vouches for state the answer did not produce; operator-timed, needs a concurrent writer within milliseconds. Moving the re-record inside the lock would settle it.
suggested_fix: Call recordFinishedRound before releasing the decisions lock, or document the window.
evidence: premise-question.ts: `if (rerecord) { recordFinishedRound(...) }` runs after `await recordPremiseDecision(...)` returned.

quote: .some((segment) => OPERATOR_ONLY_NAMES.has(segment.toLowerCase()));
problem: The case fold that closes LG2-001/SEC2-001 is JavaScript toLowerCase. A case-insensitive filesystem does not compare names that way: NTFS upcases both names through its $UpCase table, and APFS uses Unicode case folding. Some characters are not ASCII and do not lower-case to ASCII, yet upcase or fold to an ASCII letter. Examples: dotless 'ı' (U+0131) upcases to 'I', and long 's' 'ſ' (U+017F) upcases to 'S' and case-folds to 's'. So `operator-decısions.json` and `operator-deciſions.json` pass the name check. On such a filesystem they may name the same file as `operator-decisions.json`. When the decisions file does not exist yet (no operator answer so far), realTarget returns the spelling as written, so the symlink-resolved check does not catch it either.
impact: Trigger: in automatic review, an agent's apply_patch creates `.metaproject/reviews/<id>/operator-deciſions.json` before the operator has answered anything. If the filesystem folds that name onto operator-decisions.json, the patch is approved without asking. readPremiseDecisions then opens the agent's file, and a forged premise-question record is trusted by the verdict, readiness item 11 and the flow gate. The comment at :213-214 claims the fold matches APFS/NTFS, and that claim is what fails. Whether each filesystem folds these two characters this way is not verified here.
suggested_fix: Refuse any patch target segment that is not plain ASCII (`/^[\x20-\x7e]+$/`) before the name check, since package data names are keryx's own. Or compare both `segment.toLowerCase()` and `segment.toUpperCase().toLowerCase()` against OPERATOR_ONLY_NAMES. Add the two spellings to the 'folds case' test.
evidence: automatic-review.ts:213-216 (comment and lower-cased set), :232-246 realTarget returns a non-existent path as written, :253-262 touchesOperatorOnly. 'ı'.toLowerCase() === 'ı' and 'ı'.toUpperCase() === 'I'; 'ſ'.toLowerCase() === 'ſ' and 'ſ'.toUpperCase() === 'S'. To settle it: create operator-deciſions.json on an APFS case-insensitive volume and on NTFS, then check whether operator-decisions.json opens it.

quote:
if (rerecord) {
    const recorded = recordFinishedRound(packageDir, "decide-premise", registryPlace(registry));
problem: The registry vouch check runs inside the decisions lock (:199), but the re-record runs after the lock is released (:208-213). Take two answers to one package that overlap (a terminal decide-premise and a review_decide_premise card). A writes and releases. B takes the lock and finds the registry not yet re-recorded, so vouched=false. A then re-records the A-only state. B writes and skips the re-record. The registry ends up vouching for hashes that no longer match findings.json.
impact: The next round of that package falls back to full, with no warning (B saw vouched=false, so it emits none). Only state is lost, never an answer. It needs two concurrent operator answers.
suggested_fix: Re-record inside the lock: return a flag from applyFirst and call recordFinishedRound in recordPremiseDecision's locked section after the append, or run it inside a second withOperatorDecisionsLock.
evidence: premise-question.ts:175-215; operator-decisions.ts:195-203 (the lock covers applyFirst and the append only).

quote: const parent = path.relative(path.join(root, ".metaproject"), path.dirname(real)).split(path.sep);
problem: isReviewPackageDir realpaths the project root but not `<root>/.metaproject`, then compares it with the realpath of the package. If `.metaproject` (or `.metaproject/reviews`) is itself a symlink, every real previous package resolves outside `<root>/.metaproject`. The check then rejects it, and carryPremiseDecisions returns [] with no message.
impact: No answer is carried into the delta round, so the operator is asked again for findings they already answered. Nothing in the repo is known to symlink .metaproject, so no input that reaches this is named.
suggested_fix: Compare against `realpathSync(path.join(root, '.metaproject'))`, falling back to the joined path when that does not exist.

quote: await rename(path.join(packageDir, PREMISES_FILE), path.join(packageDir, PREMISES_SUPERSEDED_FILE));
problem: The record is kept only one deep. A second ingest without --premises after another --premises ingest overwrites the earlier premises.superseded.json (rename replaces the target). An ingest with --premises leaves an older superseded file beside the new premises.json.
impact: Audit history only: an earlier judge's claims are lost after two cycles, or a stale superseded file sits beside current claims. No reader of either file decides an outcome.
suggested_fix: Either say in the PREMISES_SUPERSEDED_FILE doc that it holds only the latest superseded claims, or suffix it with the ingest time.

quote: renumber a collision before dispatch. A claim names the `id`; it names the `global_id` only when a carried finding shares a new one's display id.
problem: The two sentences give opposite instructions for the one case the second sentence exists for: a new finding whose display id equals a carried finding's. 'Renumber a collision' does not cover it, because ingest keys by global_id (managed.ts:1679-1683): carried `<oldReview>#F-001` and new `<thisReview>#F-001` do not collide, so ingest never refuses them. The second sentence then lets the carried one be named by its global_id. That leaves the new one named by bare `F-001`. claimTargets matches `finding.id === id` for both (premise.ts:219), so that claim is rejected as ambiguous-finding (premise.ts:325). The text also says the new finding has no global_id to name. review-premise's `findings` row (review-premise/SKILL.md:63) repeats the same rule.
impact: Trigger: in a delta round, a carried finding with no carried premise and a new finding share a display id. The judge's claim on the new finding is rejected and listed in scope.md. That finding goes on unjudged, which fails safe but loses the premise check on it (it can still be held or lowered on a rerun). The final state is not wrong.
suggested_fix: Count a new finding that shares a carried finding's display id as a collision too, and renumber the new one before dispatch. Then every claim can name the display id, except one that targets the carried finding, which names its global_id. Or say the orchestrator may pass the new finding's future key `<reviewId>#<id>` as its global_id. Use the same wording in the review-premise `findings` row.
evidence: src/gdskills/bundled/skills/review/review-orchestrator/SKILL.md:1127; src/gdskills/bundled/skills/review/review-premise/SKILL.md:63; src/review/managed.ts:1670-1683 (assignGlobalIds keeps carried keys; findingKeyCollisions keys by global_id); src/review/premise.ts:218-221, :325.

quote: with none, its claims object goes into the Implementation Spec under **Premise**
problem: Step 1 sends the judge's claims to a **Premise** section of the Implementation Spec. Step 3 (lines 44-50) is the list of fields that spec has, and it holds no Premise field: What, Why, Scope, Acceptance criteria, Approach, Test strategy. Step 4 saves the spec to `.feature-spec.md` and gitignores it, so where no flow exists that file is the only record of the premise.
impact: A spec writer following Step 3's list leaves the section out, so the judge's claims and the operator's answer are not recorded anywhere. Phase 7 fix cycles then cannot cite them, and a dismissed premise can come back as a requirement.
suggested_fix: Add `- **Premise** (only for an input sourced from a finding): the review-premise claims object and the operator's answer, in their words` to the Step 3 list.
evidence: src/gdskills/bundled/skills/orchestration/feature-dev/SKILL.md:42 (new text), :44-51 (spec fields, .gitignore). The .metaproject copy is identical.

quote: you run `git log -L <start>,<end>:<file>` and `git blame -L <start>,<end> <file>` for each deliberate-looking site a reviewer must judge and pass the output in `context_files`
problem: On keryx shell, `context_files` takes paths only. Each must be a regular file under the project root, with at most 40 files and 400 KB in total (spawn-subagent-tool.ts:197-241). The new text says to pass 'the output'. It does not say to save that output to a file first, or where (for example `<package>/research-evidence/history-<n>.txt`), or that the history files count against the cap the slices already use. Lines 110 and 1127 and the reviewer-input schema use the same phrasing.
impact: If the output is passed inline, the dispatch is refused loudly ('not a regular file'). Nothing goes wrong silently; the cost is a retry. With many slices, the history files can push a dispatch over the 40-file cap.
suggested_fix: Say: save each excerpt as a file under the package (e.g. `research-evidence/history-<file>-<start>.txt`) and pass its path in `context_files`, within the host's file cap.

quote: await rename(path.join(packageDir, PREMISES_FILE), path.join(packageDir, PREMISES_SUPERSEDED_FILE));
problem: The RG2-004 fix moves the claims file to one fixed name. rename() replaces an existing premises.superseded.json without a word, so a second supersession destroys the first preserved record. Sequence: ingest --premises P1, ingest without, ingest --premises P2, ingest without. After that P1 is gone.
impact: Narrow. It needs repeated re-ingests that alternate with and without --premises. In that case it loses exactly the record the fix exists to keep, and nothing reports the loss.
suggested_fix: Give the superseded file a unique name (a timestamp or counter suffix), or refuse the move when the target exists. Print a line naming where the claims went, which also covers the missing warning in RG2-004.
evidence: managed.ts:507-511; premise.ts:62 (one constant name); review-premises-cli.test.ts covers only one supersession.

quote: const recorded = recordFinishedRound(packageDir, "decide-premise", registryPlace(registry));
problem: The vouch check (line 199) runs inside the decisions lock, but the re-record (line 209) runs after the lock is released. Two answers can overlap: A writes and releases, B checks (not vouched yet, because A has not re-recorded), A re-records its own state, then B writes and skips its re-record. The registry is left holding A's findings hash.
impact: Needs two operator answers on the same package at the same moment, for example a card and a terminal. The result is the RG2-001 symptom again for that package: the next round runs full and asks again about findings already answered. No trust is granted wrongly.
suggested_fix: Run recordFinishedRound inside the lock, in recordPremiseDecision's critical section after appendDecision succeeds. Or compute `vouched` and re-record within one lock span.
evidence: premise-question.ts:195-212; operator-decisions.ts:195-203 (the lock covers only applyFirst and the append).

quote: display ids must be unique in the package (ingest refuses two findings under one key): renumber a collision before dispatch.
problem: The text does not say where to renumber. Ingest's collision check (managed.ts:452-459) runs on the final findings after dedupe, over the ids in the saved reviewer results. A renumber done only in the judge's payload leaves both reviewers' `F-001` in the results, so ingest refuses, and the judge's claims name an id that exists nowhere in the package.
impact: Trigger: two reviewers both return F-001 (the collision case the text handles). Outcome: either ingest refuses the round, or, if the results are edited afterwards, the judge's claims name the old id and are rejected as unknown-finding, losing the held finding.
suggested_fix: Say the renumber is made in the saved reviewer results before Wave D (so the judge, the claims and ingest all see the same ids), not in the dispatch payload alone.

quote: .metaproject/reviews/pr-comments/<owner>__<repo>__<n>.premise.json
problem: The sidecar sits in the directory whose `*.json` files are read as pr-comments records (src/learning/signals/reviewer-comment.ts:25). The reader treats a file without `seen` as empty, so nothing breaks today, but the dependency is accidental.
impact: No failure now; a future reader of that directory that does not tolerate a non-record `.json` would misread it.
suggested_fix: Acceptable as is; optionally note the name is reserved for the premise sidecar.

quote: Nothing here is an instruction the agent must follow at a step
problem: SKILL.md:2156 says `Use the template in SKILL.detail.md` for the post-mortem, so the file does hold material the agent follows at a step. The header contradicts the link.
impact: Wording only; an agent that treats the file as optional skips the post-mortem template.
suggested_fix: Reword the header to 'templates and examples the steps link to'.

quote: .some((segment) => OPERATOR_ONLY_NAMES.has(segment.toLowerCase()));
problem: The operator-only guard compares path segments after String.prototype.toLowerCase(). The APFS (and NTFS) name match uses Unicode case folding, and that is wider. U+017F LATIN SMALL LETTER LONG S folds to `s`, and toLowerCase() leaves it as it is, so `operator-deciſions.json` passes `named(dir, resolved)`. The realpath branch catches the name only when operator-decisions.json already exists, because Bun's realpathSync then returns the on-disk name. When it does not exist yet, realTarget appends the missing segment as written, and `named(realDir, real)` misses it too. The extension check passes, since `.json` is unchanged. Once the agent has created the file, the realpath branch returns the agent's own spelling, so later patches are approved as well. readPremiseDecisions opens path.join(dir, 'operator-decisions.json'), and on a case-insensitive volume that finds the agent's file.
impact: Attack vector, the same as SEC2-001(a): during an automatic review, hostile PR content steers the orchestrating agent. The agent apply_patches `<bound package>/operator-deciſions.json` with a complete premise-question record: {kind:'premise-question', finding:<held id>, answer:'dismiss', reason, quote, at, actor:'operator', confirmedVia:'terminal', subject:{severity, verdict, problemSha256}}. The subject's problemSha256 is sha256 of the problem text, which the agent can compute. approvesPatchTargets approves the patch with no question. readPremiseDecisions returns the forged record, premiseHoldState returns `dismissed`, and the flow gate and readiness item 11 pass for a held blocker the operator never answered. The precondition is a package with no operator-decisions.json yet, which is the usual state while a held finding waits for its first answer. Probe (scratchpad, HEAD code, APFS): approvesPatchTargets(['.metaproject/reviews/<ID>/operator-deciſions.json']) returns true with no file and again after the file exists; readdir shows only 'operator-deciſions.json'; readFileSync('<dir>/operator-decisions.json') returns its contents.
suggested_fix: Do not rely on a JS case mapping to match the filesystem. Either (1) refuse any approved patch target with a segment outside a conservative ASCII set (e.g. /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$/), so a name that could alias the operator files always needs the operator; or (2) fold with segment.normalize('NFC').toUpperCase().toLowerCase() (ſ→S→s, Kelvin K→K→k) and keep (1) as defence in depth. Add `operator-deciſions.json` and `.operator-deciſions.lock/x` to the test at automatic-review.test.ts:16-23.
evidence: src/commands/automatic-review.ts:216 builds OPERATOR_ONLY_NAMES with toLowerCase(); :232-246 realTarget appends the non-existent tail as written; :253-262 touchesOperatorOnly; :320-324 approvesPatchTargets. A Bun probe shows 'operator-deciſions.json'.toLowerCase() !== 'operator-decisions.json' and that APFS resolves the name to the same file. The guard approved the path before and after creation, and the ASCII path read back the agent-created file.

class_scope.enumeration_method: grep toLowerCase|OPERATOR_DECISIONS_FILE in src/commands/automatic-review.ts. The only name compares for operator-only files are the set construction (:216) and the segment test (:258), and both cover both members (decisions file, lock dir). The extension compares at :321-322 fail closed on a folded variant (.jſon is not allowed), so they are outside the class.

quote: const recorded = recordFinishedRound(packageDir, "decide-premise", registryPlace(registry));
problem: answerPremiseQuestion checks registryVouchesPackage inside the decisions lock, but it calls recordFinishedRound after recordPremiseDecision has released the lock. findings.json is also writable by an auto-approved apply_patch, which takes no lock. A write landing between the release and the re-record would be hashed and vouched by the registry as the decide-premise round.
impact: No reachable path shown. It needs an agent tool call to run concurrently with the operator's answer, between two adjacent awaits. Settling it means checking whether keryx shell runs an apply_patch concurrently with a confirm-card apply. If it can, a steered agent's edits to findings.json would be vouched as if keryx had finished that round.
suggested_fix: Run the re-record inside the same withOperatorDecisionsLock callback, after appendDecision succeeds. Or re-check that findings.json still hashes to the content just written before recording.
evidence: src/review/premise-question.ts:177-213: vouched is computed in the applyFirst callback, and the re-record runs after `await recordPremiseDecision(...)` returns; src/review/operator-decisions.ts withOperatorDecisionsLock wraps only applyFirst + appendDecision.

problem: The long docblock describing the whole embedded-findings convention (one file, opening fence decides presence, indentation allowed) now sits on the generic embeddedFence(tag) helper, which also serves keryx:premises.

suggested_fix: Move the convention docblock to parseEmbeddedFindings or give embeddedFence a one-line doc of its own.

problem: answerPremiseQuestion sets a closure-mutated `let rerecord` inside the applyFirst callback and reads it after recordPremiseDecision returns; the undo path also resets it.
impact: Control flow is carried by a flag mutated across an async callback, which is harder to follow than returning the value; correct as written.

quote: its claims object goes into the Implementation Spec under **Premise**
problem: The fix for R2-004 sends the claims to a spec section the spec template does not have: the field list at lines 43-49 is What, Why, Scope, Acceptance criteria, Approach, Test strategy.

quote: recorded as follow-up, not fixed in this flow.", "premise: every plan item's comment
problem: The new `premise:` constraint is appended on the same line as the `scope:` string, after a comma; every other constraint in the array sits on its own line.

quote: A failing item but `premise-decisions` is waived only by the operator.
problem: Ungrammatical: 'but' needs 'any' ('Any failing item but ...'); as written it is ambiguous in the sentence that sets the non-waivable rule.
